# Expert report — Digital PR, podcasts & earned awareness

# Earned Awareness for SMD Services: Digital PR, Sourcing, Podcasts & Founder Thought Leadership

## 1. The current playbook, applied to SMD

Earned awareness in 2026 has consolidated around three formats that journalists actually reward: **original-data studies, expert reactive commentary (newsjacking), and free tools/calculators** ([Reflect Digital](https://www.reflectdigital.co.uk/blog/8-digital-pr-trends-to-watch-in-2026)). The HARO era ended — Connectively shut December 2024 — and sourcing fragmented across **Source of Sources (Shankman's free successor), Qwoted, Featured.com, SourceBottle, and #journorequest on X** ([Prezly](https://www.prezly.com/academy/the-best-haro-alternatives), [Reporter Outreach](https://www.reporteroutreach.com/blog/haro-alternatives)). The structural shift that matters for us: **proprietary data is the entry ticket.** Data-driven angles see a ~47% journalist pickup rate versus ~8% for generic "future of AI" pitches, and journalist fatigue on generic AI pitches is at crisis levels — reporters receive hundreds weekly ([Reporter Outreach](https://www.reporteroutreach.com/blog/digital-pr-statistics), [BuzzStream](https://www.buzzstream.com/blog/state-of-digital-pr-2026/)).

This is the crux of your mandate's question. "AI that runs a small business's back office" is **not** itself a differentiated hook — it is the single most over-pitched story in B2B right now (59% of PR pros rank AI their top priority). What a generic consultancy can never produce, and what SMD uniquely sits on, is **proprietary data about invisible SMB operational pain**: the 357-entity signal engine, the job-posting/permit/review pipelines, and the enrichment layer already generate exactly the dataset journalists peg stories to. The earned-media unlock is not the AI claim — it is **the evidence**. SMD can say "here is what operational drag actually looks like across 350 Arizona businesses," and back it. That is the angle no competitor can copy.

A second, rarer asset: **SMD runs its own back office on its own Operator** (Crane handles SMD's inbound/outbound email autonomously). "We eat our own dog food" is a durable, demonstrable founder narrative — not a claim, a running system.

## 2. Concrete tactics

1. **Reactive sourcing, daily.** Put Scott on Source of Sources, Qwoted, and Featured.com; monitor #journorequest. Answer queries on SMB operations, AI adoption, automation-without-layoffs. This is the cheapest, fastest path to a real backlink and a quote. Win rate is low — treat it as volume.
2. **One proprietary data study as the linkable asset.** Anonymized, aggregate, from the signal-engine data: _"The Operational Drag Index: what 350 Arizona small businesses reveal about where owners lose time."_ Slice it by the 12 verticals so each pack gets its own data peg (law-firm intake lag, dental recall gaps, etc.). This is the single highest-leverage move — it feeds trade press, podcasts, and SEO simultaneously.
3. **Vertical trade-press pitching.** The 12 packs each map to a trade outlet (e.g., dental, RIA, property-management press). Pitch the vertical-specific data cut, not the firm. National reach here serves the national Operator packs perfectly.
4. **Local Phoenix earned media.** Pitch _Phoenix Business Journal_ and _AZ Big Media_ on the local angle: a Phoenix firm building AI back-office workers for Main Street businesses, founder eating his own dog food. This serves the **Arizona-local consulting** funnel that national media cannot.
5. **Founder thought leadership on LinkedIn.** A steady cadence of concrete, data-backed posts — not hot takes. Edelman-LinkedIn found 75% of decision-makers researched something new because of thought leadership, and 70% of C-suite reconsidered a vendor; yet only 15% rate the quality "very good/excellent" ([Edelman](https://www.edelman.com/expertise/Business-Marketing/2025-b2b-thought-leadership-report)). The quality gap is the opening.
6. **Targeted podcast guesting** on SMB-owner and vertical-operator shows (not generic "AI" shows). Topic-aligned pitches reply at 2–3x category-only pitches ([CastFox](https://www.castfox.net/blog/how-to-find-podcasts-to-pitch-as-a-guest-2026)).

## 3. Benchmarks (external — do not treat as SMD targets)

- **Backlink cost:** average quality link ~$370–500; high-authority (DR 70+) $800–1,500; 54% of marketers pay >$300/link ([iNet Ventures](https://inetventures.com/blog/how-much-do-backlinks-cost), [LinkBuild](https://linkbuild.agency/digital-pr-statistics/)).
- **Digital PR campaign performance:** ~67% response rate, average DA 72, ~42 referring domains per campaign — versus 2–7% success for transactional link-building outreach ([Reporter Outreach](https://www.reporteroutreach.com/blog/digital-pr-statistics)).
- **Spend norms:** most run $3,000–10,000/mo; small businesses can start a focused effort at ~$1,500/mo ([Softtrix](https://www.softtrix.com/blog/link-building-cost/)).
- **Reactive PR speed:** newsjacking can earn high-DA links within 24–48 hours ([Reflect Digital](https://www.reflectdigital.co.uk/blog/8-digital-pr-trends-to-watch-in-2026)).
- **Podcasts:** ~10% average guest-to-client conversion, up to 48% on strategic invites; reply rates 30–50% on entry-tier lists; 77% of marketers call podcasts among the most effective content; estimated 527% ROI — **but it takes 9–12 months to materialize** ([Prospeo](https://prospeo.io/s/podcast-lead-generation), [Martal](https://martal.ca/lead-generation-statistics-lb/)).

## 4. Honest fit assessment

**Speed to first lead: slow, and you must say so.** Digital PR and podcasts compound; podcast ROI explicitly lags 9–12 months. This channel **will not produce the leads-NOW that the pre-launch pressure demands.** It is the wrong tool for that job — your ~100 enriched-and-drafted outbound leads sitting untouched are the near-term play, not this.

**Where it fails for SMD specifically:**

- **Attribution.** SMB owners don't click podcast show-notes into a SaaS funnel. Expecting clean lead attribution will make this look like a failure when it's actually working at the awareness layer.
- **Geography mismatch.** National earned media is wasted on Arizona-only consulting. Only the **Operator packs** and **local Phoenix press** convert this channel's reach into pipeline. Be deliberate about which asset serves which funnel.
- **Generic-AI trap.** If the pitch leads with "AI employee," it drowns in the fatigue pile. The proprietary data, not the AI, must lead every pitch.
- **Founder bandwidth.** Podcasting and TL run on Scott's time — the same scarce close-calendar that ADR 0039 names the binding constraint. Earned awareness competes with the thing that actually closes revenue.

**What has to be true for it to work:** SMD produces and stands behind a real data study; pitches are vertical-specific and data-led; and leadership accepts this as a **compounding brand/SEO asset measured over quarters**, not a lead spigot measured in weeks.

**Fit verdict:** A strong _secondary, compounding_ channel — particularly because the proprietary-data moat is genuine and uncopyable. A poor _primary, near-term_ channel. Run it in parallel with outbound; never instead of it.

## 5. Phased ramp (sequence, not calendar)

- **Initial moves:** Stand up reactive sourcing (Source of Sources, Qwoted, Featured, #journorequest). Start the founder LinkedIn cadence. Pitch Phoenix Business Journal / AZ Big Media on the local + dog-food angle. Cheapest, fastest mentions; warms the well.
- **Early build:** Produce the Operational Drag Index from signal-engine data, sliced by vertical. Build its landing page (no published dollars; voice laws apply — no em dashes). Pitch the vertical cuts to trade press. Begin topic-aligned podcast guesting.
- **Maturing:** Turn the Index into a recurring quarterly release (a reason for journalists to come back). Scale podcast cadence on vertical-operator shows. Let accumulated backlinks compound the SEO of `/packs/*` and `/book`, so organic search captures AI-in-SMB queries and feeds the assessment.

## 6. How a touched prospect reaches the assessment

The path is **soft, single-destination, and always the one front door.** No earned placement carries a hard sell. A data-study reader or podcast listener lands on a **vertical pack page** (`/packs/law-firm`, etc.) or the Index landing page — content that demonstrates the operational read, then offers the **assessment at `/book`** as the natural next step ("we'll do a read of where your team's time actually goes"). On podcasts, Scott frames the assessment itself as the offer — the collaborative diagnostic, not a pitch. Backlinks do double duty: they lift `/book` and `/packs/*` in organic search, so the channel both refers directly and strengthens the funnel everything else points at. The give-away discipline mirrors ADR 0039 — earn the awareness, withhold the verdict, route to the human-owned close.
